summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch recounted Joe Goss' American career, including his 1876 Kentucky fight with Tom Allen, won by Goss on a foul after 21 rounds, after which Allen jumped his bail and left for England.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Saturday, March 28, 1885, page 11. article.json has no focus field.

facts.fact: Joe Goss came to America in April 1876 partly to make another match with Allen, then generally regarded as the rightful champion; Allen accepted his challenge for $2,500 a side
Allen fought Joe Goss on Sept. 7, 1876, on Kentucky soil, the ring first pitched in Kenton County and then moved to Boone County; after 21 rounds in 48 minutes Goss was given the fight on a foul
Indicted by the Kenton County grand jury, Allen jumped his $3,000 bail and crossed into Canada, from where he went by steamer to England
